record_identity.title: AI-generated doctor deepfakes used NHS branding to market weight-loss patches

incident_identity.historical_event_name: AI-generated doctor deepfakes used NHS branding to market weight-loss patches
incident_identity.date_basis: The NHS trust warning and BBC reporting establish that the deepfake advertisements were circulating by 9 January 2026; an earlier first-publication date is not established.

summary: Videos circulating on social media promoted weight-loss patches through supposed doctors claiming affiliation with Guy’s and St Thomas’ NHS Foundation Trust. The Trust said the people named and pictured were not its staff and the endorsements were fraudulent. It warned the public on 9 January2026 and said it was seeking removal. Full Fact later reported fake names and images, misleading hospital branding and thousands of Facebook views. Its checks identified signs of AI generation; purchaser losses and medical injuries were not reported.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: The originating Trust warning and Full Fact response identify fictional doctor names/images and false institutional affiliation. They do not identify an appropriated real clinician’s likeness or voice. Full Fact describes fabricated hospital signage, including separate Mayo Clinic branding, circulation and attributed watermark checks. A reported positive watermark check on one video does not attribute every video to a generator; non-detection on another does not exclude AI. The warning and request for takedown do not establish completed removal, purchases or injury. Health efficacy was outside Full Fact’s adjudication.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: False medical and institutional authority supplied commercial solicitation and deceptive trust cues. A generator-side authority failure over a real identifiable person is not established and its former mapping is withdrawn. Institutional false attribution and public correction remain material. Human promotional intent is not an independently pursued model objective. Warning and removal efforts are distinct from successful containment. The institutional correction supports minor bounded reputational injury. Audience size does not establish meaningful deterioration of standing or patient harm.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: Fictional professional identities can borrow real institutional trust to influence health-related purchases. Institutional impersonation, real-person likeness appropriation and verified purchaser harm require separate evidence.
